rule: General guidance written by the build on 2026-11-01 from official transport operator, government and tourism board pages read that day (listed per row). Each row is checked for one main city or area; other cities differ. No fares or prices. A null field was not on the pages read and shows as not sure. Systems change: verify locally.

countries.transit: In Dubai, one nol card pays for the metro, tram, buses and water transport (water taxi, ferry and abra).
countries.taxi: Dubai taxis are among the services a nol card can pay for.
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping, hours and airport links were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: SUBE is the prepaid card for city buses (colectivos), the Buenos Aires subte, trains and ferries. On buses, tap and tell the driver where you are going; on trains, tap in and out or pay the maximum fare.
countries.contactless_note: Contactless Visa and Mastercard cards, including foreign ones, and NFC phones can be tapped on SUBE buses; discounts apply only to SUBE cards.
countries.recheck_reason: Taxis, hours and airport links were not on the official pages read.

countries.transit: In Vienna, validate timed tickets before you travel: at the blue machines at U-Bahn and S-Bahn entrances, or inside trams and buses. Night buses are included.
countries.contactless_note: Tap+Ride pilot since 28 May 2026: tap a Visa or Mastercard card or a phone at devices near the ticket machines in nine U-Bahn stations for a single ticket; no tap-out.
countries.airport: The City Airport Train (CAT) and Vienna Airport Bus sell their own tickets. With a Wiener Linien ticket, add a one-way ticket for the part outside the core zone.
countries.recheck_reason: Taxis and service hours were not on the official pages read; Tap+Ride is a pilot.

countries.transit: Sydney, the Blue Mountains, Central Coast, Hunter and Illawarra share one fare system. Contactless fares match Opal fares and benefits.
countries.contactless_note: Tap a credit or debit card, phone or watch instead of an Opal card.
countries.taxi: At Sydney Airport, taxis wait at organised ranks outside the terminals.
countries.airport: Sydney: trains about every 10 minutes from the domestic and international stations, about 5am to midnight; Central is about 8 minutes from the domestic station. Pay by Opal or contactless card; an airport station access fee is added.
countries.recheck_reason: Only Sydney was checked; other cities have their own systems.

countries.transit: In Toronto, tap on PRESTO readers on all TTC buses, streetcars and subway fare gates.
countries.contactless_note: Credit and debit cards, including on a phone or watch, can be tapped on PRESTO readers for adult fares.
countries.recheck_reason: Only Toronto transit was checked; taxis and airport links were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: Trains, buses and boats share one set of passes. The Swiss Travel Pass gives unlimited travel on consecutive days, including public transport in more than 90 towns and cities; the Half Fare Card gives up to half off.
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping, taxis and airport links were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: In Santiago, the bip! card pays for buses, Metro and MetroTren (Alameda-Nos). Buy it at bip! centres, Metro and MetroTren ticket offices and authorised shops.
countries.contactless_note: Since 13 February 2026, Metro and MetroTren (Alameda-Nos) accept Visa and Mastercard credit, debit and prepaid cards and phone wallets; buses are not listed.
countries.recheck_reason: Taxis, hours and airport links were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: In Prague, buy tickets from machines, the PID Lítačka app or touchscreen terminals inside trams, buses and trolleybuses. Validate a paper ticket once, before boarding or entering the metro.
countries.contactless_note: Terminals on trams, buses and trolleybuses and touchscreen machines sell tickets by contactless card; button machines take coins only.
countries.airport: Bus 59 to Veleslavín (metro A), bus 100 to Zličín (metro B), or the AE Airport Express to the Main Railway Station (its own fare; 24- and 72-hour tickets not valid). Night lines 907 and 910.
countries.recheck_reason: Taxis and service hours were not on the official pages read.

countries.transit: In Berlin, buy a ticket before you ride (app, station machines, shops) or from the bus driver. Validate paper tickets in the small boxes on platforms or in vehicles; an unvalidated ticket counts as invalid.
countries.contactless_note: Bus drivers sell tickets cashless and contactless; newer tram ticket machines take debit or credit cards and phone wallets.
countries.hours: Night buses N1 to N9 replace U-Bahn lines U1 to U9 at night.
countries.recheck_reason: Taxis and airport links were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: In Barcelona, the T-casual is a 10-journey ticket for one person, held on a T-mobilitat card, an NFC phone or an anonymous card.
countries.airport: The T-casual is not valid at the Aeroport T1 and T2 metro stations on line L9 Sud; check the airport ticket before you travel.
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping, taxis and hours were not on the official page read; the Madrid metro site could not be read.

countries.transit: In Paris and Île-de-France, Navigo Easy is a reusable pass for occasional trips, sold at ticket offices. Load single t+ tickets, ticket books or day passes onto it.
countries.airport: OrlyBus and RoissyBus tickets can be loaded onto Navigo Easy.
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping, taxis and hours were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: In London, pay as you go with a contactless card or device, or an Oyster card, instead of buying a ticket first. Fares are capped daily and weekly.
countries.contactless_note: Contactless cards and devices pay as you go, at the same capped fares as Oyster.
countries.taxi: Use a black cab or a pre-booked minicab from a reputable company; minicabs must be booked, and never use unauthorised drivers. Each Heathrow arrival hall has a taxi desk and rank.
countries.airport: Heathrow: Heathrow Express to Paddington (fastest), the Elizabeth line to central and east London, the Piccadilly line (slower), coaches to Victoria, and the N9 night bus.

countries.transit: Athens has three metro lines (Line 1 runs Kifissia to Piraeus), a tram, buses and trolleybuses. Ath.ena tickets and cards work on all of them; a single ticket lasts 90 minutes, except on airport services.
countries.hours: Metro daily 5am to midnight, lines 2 and 3 until 2am on Fridays and Saturdays; tram 5:30am to 1am; most buses 5am to midnight.
countries.taxi: Taxis are yellow; make sure the meter is on when you get in.
countries.airport: Airport express buses run 24 hours to Syntagma Square, Piraeus port and the KTEL Kifissos bus station.
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping was not on the official page read.

countries.transit: The MTR covers all major districts; buses, trams, green minibuses and the Star Ferry also take Octopus. On trams, board at the back and pay at the front when you leave. Red minibuses are paid when you get off.
countries.contactless_note: Visa, Mastercard and UnionPay contactless cards (not UnionPay debit) and phones work at MTR gates with the contactless symbol, including Airport Express; not on Light Rail or MTR Bus.
countries.taxi: Taxis are metered. Red taxis serve most of Hong Kong, green the New Territories and blue Lantau Island; ask for a printed receipt.
countries.airport: Airport Express is the fastest, about 24 minutes to Hong Kong Island. Airbus A routes and city buses serve Hong Kong Island, Kowloon and the New Territories; taxis wait at the Arrivals Hall.

countries.transit: In Zagreb, ZET runs day and night trams and buses. Validate single and daily tickets when you board.
countries.recheck_reason: Where to buy tickets, bank-card use, taxis and airport links were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: MRT Jakarta accepts contactless bank cards since 29 July 2026, so a dedicated transit card is not needed on the MRT.
countries.contactless_note: Visa and Mastercard contactless cards work on MRT Jakarta; not yet confirmed for TransJakarta buses or the LRT.
countries.recheck_reason: Only the MRT was checked; buses, taxis and airport links were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: In Dublin, city buses (Dublin Bus and Go-Ahead Ireland), Luas trams, DART and Commuter Rail all take TFI Leap cards. The Leap Visitor Card gives unlimited travel for a set period.
countries.taxi: Taxis, hackneys and limousines are licensed by the National Transport Authority, which offers a tool to check a licence.
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping and airport links were not on the official pages read.

countries.transit: The Delhi Metro serves Delhi, Gurgaon and Noida. A stored-value Travel Card suits repeat trips; a Tourist Card gives 1 or 3 days of unlimited travel (refundable deposit).
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping, hours, taxis and the airport line were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: Strætó runs buses across greater Reykjavík, most every 15 minutes at peak times and every 30 minutes otherwise. Capital-area buses take no cash.
countries.contactless_note: Tap a Visa, Mastercard or phone wallet on board: one tap buys one adult fare, valid 75 minutes. Rural buses still take cash or card.
countries.recheck_reason: Taxis and Keflavík airport links were not on the official pages read.

countries.transit: In Rome, ATAC buses, trams, trolleybuses and metro lines accept tap&go. On surface lines one tap covers changes for 100 minutes; a metro ride counts as one journey.
countries.contactless_note: Tap a contactless credit, debit or prepaid card, phone or watch and wait for the green light. Show the reader only one card, and tap again each time you change vehicle.
countries.recheck_reason: Ticket names, taxis and airport links were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: Trains in the big cities run every few minutes; rural services are fewer. Tap an IC card at the gate to enter and again to exit, or buy a paper ticket at the station machine. Look for the IC logo: highway buses, for one, may not take IC cards.
countries.taxi: Taxis are metered by distance, with a surcharge from 10pm to 5am. A red sign means free. Doors open and close automatically. Cards are generally accepted in big-city taxis; carry cash in the countryside.
countries.airport: Narita: ask the driver for the fixed taxi fare to central Tokyo zones. Haneda: flat-rate taxis to most of Tokyo. Kansai and Itami: shared taxi shuttles.
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping and airport rail links were not on the official pages read.

countries.transit: In Kuala Lumpur, Rapid KL's LRT, MRT, BRT, Monorail and buses take the MyRapid TnG card, which pays a lower cashless fare. Reload it at stations and many shops.
countries.recheck_reason: The operator pages read are older; bank-card tapping, taxis and airport links were not on them.

countries.transit: Check in when you board the tram, bus, metro or train and check out at your destination, with a contactless bank card or phone (OVpay). No app or registration needed.
countries.contactless_note: Contactless Maestro, V PAY, Mastercard and Visa cards and phone wallets; on GVB lines fares are capped per day.
countries.taxi: At Schiphol, use the official taxi rank, avoid drivers who approach you inside the airport, and check the meter is running.
countries.airport: Schiphol: trains about eight times an hour to Amsterdam Centraal (about 17 minutes) from the station under the terminal; check in at the yellow readers in Schiphol Plaza. Bus 397 runs to Museumplein and Leidseplein, N97 at night; no cash on the bus.

countries.transit: In Oslo, Ruter tickets cover buses, trams, metro, ferries (not the Bygdøy ferry) and local trains. Zone 1 covers central Oslo. Buy before boarding in the Ruter app or at kiosks; trams and the metro sell no tickets on board.
countries.airport: Trips to Oslo Airport need a ticket covering more zones; the Oslo Pass covers the airport.
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping, taxis and hours were not on the official pages read.

countries.transit: In Auckland, AT buses, trains and most AT ferries share one fare system. Tag on when you board or enter a station, and tag off when you get off.
countries.contactless_note: Contactless Visa, Mastercard, UnionPay and American Express cards and phone wallets work on AT buses, trains and most AT ferries, not Waiheke or tourist ferries. Use the same card to tag on and off.
countries.recheck_reason: Only Auckland was checked; taxis and airport links were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: In Lisbon, load single tickets, day tickets or Zapping (pay-as-you-go credit) onto a navegante card; Zapping works across Carris, Metro, CP and other operators. Validate every journey before boarding.
countries.contactless_note: A contactless bank card pays for a Metro trip directly at the gate validators.
countries.hours: Lisbon Metro runs daily from 06:30 to 01:00 (last train from each end of the line).
countries.recheck_reason: Taxis and airport links were not on the official pages read.

countries.transit: MRT, LRT and public buses charge by distance. Tap in and tap out with the same card or device; changes within set time limits add no boarding charge.
countries.contactless_note: Contactless Visa, Mastercard and American Express cards work, foreign ones too (turn on overseas use). Cash works only on buses, exact fare.
countries.taxi: Changi Airport has taxi stands in the arrival areas of every terminal, running 24 hours.
countries.airport: Changi: MRT to Tanah Merah for the East West Line or to Expo for the Downtown Line, first train 5:31am (5:59am Sundays and holidays), last about 11:18pm. Public buses leave from the terminals; after midnight, taxis and app-booked cars.

countries.transit: From 1 June 2026, Bangkok's MRT lines take contactless bank cards; one card works on all four MRT lines.
countries.contactless_note: EMV contactless cards with the contactless symbol, Thai or foreign (Visa, Mastercard and others), pay the adult fare on the MRT.
countries.recheck_reason: Only the MRT was checked; the BTS Skytrain, taxis and airport links were not on the official pages read.

countries.transit: In Taipei, the Metro and Taipei and New Taipei City buses take EasyCard or iPASS, which also pay for shared bikes. Single-journey, one-day and 24, 48 and 72-hour tickets are sold at stations.
countries.recheck_reason: Bank-card tapping, taxis and the airport MRT were not on the official page read.

countries.transit: In New York City, tap a contactless card, phone, wearable or OMNY card at subway turnstiles and on buses. Use the same card or device for a free transfer; a weekly fare cap applies.
countries.contactless_note: Tap to pay works on the subway and buses, including Select Bus Service.
countries.airport: JFK: app-based rides use designated pick-up areas; the AirTrain links the terminals with Federal Circle for hotel shuttles.
countries.recheck_reason: Only New York City was checked; taxi details were not on the official pages read.

countries.transit: Gautrain trains and buses take a Gautrain Card or a contactless bank card; no cash on trains, buses or at parking. Use the same card for the whole trip.
countries.contactless_note: Contactless bank cards work on Gautrain trains and buses; do not tap out of a bus with a bank card (it charges two trips).
countries.airport: OR Tambo International Airport has a Gautrain station; Gautrain buses do not serve the airport.
countries.recheck_reason: Only the Gautrain was checked; city buses and taxis were not on the official page read.
